title: From gigawatts to critical mineral demands for EU solar and wind - Nature Energy
gist: Only the abstract is accessible (paywalled preview, mostly references). A scenario study of EU27 solar, onshore and offshore wind targets through 2050 finds unprecedented demand for copper, zinc, silicon and rare earths, with offshore-wind-heavy pathways keeping rare earth exposure near full-target levels (69.2 kilotonnes).

themes.theme: Mineral demand of EU renewable targets

insights.claim: Expanding solar, onshore and offshore wind across the EU's 27 member states through 2050 is projected to generate unprecedented demand for copper, zinc, silicon and rare earth elements.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Legally binding EU deployment targets imply a structural demand bid for base metals, silicon and rare earths.

insights.claim: Supply-chain exposure of the EU transition depends strongly on which technology pathway is chosen, based on three scenario projections.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Mineral risk is a function of the solar/onshore/offshore mix, not just total gigawatts.

themes.theme: Offshore wind and rare earth lock-in

insights.claim: Offshore-wind-prioritizing pathways keep rare earth exposure near full-target levels (69.2 kilotonnes) even when solar and onshore deployment falls short, because rare earths are technologically embedded in direct-driven turbine generators.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Rare earth demand is sticky to offshore wind and does not scale down with other shortfalls, implying persistent exposure to rare earth (largely non-EU) supply.

themes.theme: Mineral security as feasibility constraint and policy remedies

insights.claim: The authors reframe the clean energy transition as a continental materials procurement challenge in which mineral security acts as a binding feasibility constraint on climate goals.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Supports the view that materials access, not just capital or permitting, caps EU renewables build-out.

insights.claim: The authors recommend institutionalizing material stress tests in national deployment plans, establishing strategic component reserves and actively securing international midstream processing partnerships.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Points to policy tailwinds for stockpiling, component reserves and midstream processing partnerships outside the EU.
